hints: Focus on what must happen first for a precipitate to form, the C-X bond must break to release a halide ion for silver to capture.
Recall how the three silver halides behave differently in ammonia, AgCl dissolves easily, AgBr needs concentrated ammonia, but AgI stays solid.
Check each haloalkane in turn to see which halide it would release and whether that silver precipitate would dissolve in concentrated ammonia.
walkthrough:
**Understand the test**

Warming a halogenoalkane with aqueous silver nitrate causes slow hydrolysis. The halide ion released then meets silver ions to make a precipitate.

$$\text{R-X + H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow \text{R-OH + X}^- + \text{H}^+$$
$$\text{Ag}^+\text{(aq) + X}^-\text{(aq)} \rightarrow \text{AgX(s)}$$

**Use ammonia solubility to identify the halide**

This is the classic way to tell the silver halides apart. AgCl dissolves in dilute ammonia, AgBr only dissolves in concentrated ammonia, and AgI does not dissolve even in concentrated ammonia.

**Apply to the three compounds**

1-bromopropane would give $\text{Br}^-$, so $\text{AgBr}$ which does dissolve in concentrated ammonia. 2-chlorobutane would give $\text{Cl}^-$, so $\text{AgCl}$ which also dissolves in concentrated ammonia.

$$\text{1 gives AgBr, 2 gives AgCl, both dissolve}$$

**Rule out the iodide**

2-iodo-2-methylpropane would give $\text{I}^-$, so $\text{AgI}$ which is insoluble even in concentrated ammonia. It would give a precipitate, but it would not dissolve.

So only 1 and 2 fit both observations.

options.A: Incorrect because it includes all three. Statements 1 and 2 are correct, but 3 gives AgI which does not dissolve in concentrated ammonia, so 3 must be excluded.
options.B: Correct because only 1 and 2 fit. 1-bromopropane gives AgBr and 2-chlorobutane gives AgCl, both of which dissolve in concentrated aqueous ammonia.
options.C: Incorrect because it includes 3 and excludes 1. Compound 3 gives AgI which remains as a yellow precipitate in concentrated ammonia, while compound 1 correctly gives soluble AgBr and should be included.
options.D: Incorrect because it includes only 1. While 1-bromopropane is correct, 2-chlorobutane is also correct since AgCl dissolves readily in concentrated (and even dilute) ammonia.
